c.tagline: Gateway to the Japan Alps — the black 'Crow Castle' and wasabi-fed mountain streams.

taxi.fareNote: Taxis are metered and reliable but pricey; there is no Uber ride-share, and apps such as GO and DiDi simply dispatch regular metered taxis. For sightseeing most visitors use the Town Sneaker loop bus, Alpico buses and the Matsumoto Dentetsu line instead.

emergency.note: Dial 110 for police and 119 for fire and ambulance; 119 operators can often arrange English-language support.

hood_desc: The castle district north of the Metoba river, home to the black National-Treasure Matsumoto Castle, the city museum and municipal offices; central and packed with the must-see sights.
A preserved merchant street of white-walled kura storehouses now full of craft shops, sake breweries and cafes; atmospheric and full of boutique browsing.
The riverside 'Frog Street' lined with tiny stalls, antique shops and the Yohashira Shrine; quirky, characterful and best explored by day.
The modern transport hub around Matsumoto Station, with the main hotels, department stores and bus terminals; the convenient walkable base for arrivals and onward trips.
A historic hot-spring quarter in the north-eastern foothills, once the bath of the Matsumoto castle lords, with ryokan and public baths; quiet and restful.

water.note: Tap water is excellent Alpine-sourced and safe everywhere.

transit.hours: The Town Sneaker and city buses run roughly 8:00am-6/7pm; trains run from early morning to around midnight, after which taxis are the only option.
transit.note: The castle, Nakamachi and Nawate are all an easy walk from the station, so most visitors only need buses for Asama Onsen or trains onward to the Alps, Kamikochi and Nagano.
transit.pay: City buses are pay-on-board in cash (IC cards such as Suica are only slowly rolling out on Alpico buses, so carry coins); the Town Sneaker loop is ¥200 a ride or ¥500 for a day pass. JR and Matsumoto Dentetsu trains take IC cards and tickets from station machines.

bus: Matsumoto Bus Terminal (Alpico highway coaches to Tokyo/Nagoya/Osaka)
train: Matsumoto Station (JR Azusa Ltd Express to Tokyo/Shinjuku)

transit.m: Alpico airport shuttle bus to Matsumoto Station (~25 min, meets flights)
Taxi to the city centre (~20-25 min)

tip.r: Tipping is not customary in Japan and can cause confusion; excellent service is simply included in the price.
